files.why: It owns the reactive appointments list + derived conflicts, so the optimistic patch (apply new start/end + recompute conflicts immediately) and the snapshot-and-rollback on server rejection belong here.

submit() today validates then awaits the mutation and only returns after the server responds; it must apply the validated slot optimistically before awaiting rescheduleAppointment and trigger rollback + surface the error when the promise rejects.

onRescheduled currently does a full refresh() (why the new time only shows after the round-trip); it must wire the optimistic apply into useDaySchedule instead of refetching, and re-sync/rollback on rejection.
It only renders pre-submit validation errors and closes on success; it needs to surface the post-rollback server-rejection error so a failed optimistic reschedule is visible to the user.

uncertain: Whether the optimistic patch+rollback lives in useDaySchedule (list/conflict owner) with useReschedule delegating to it, versus being coordinated in DayView — the seam between the two composables is the least obvious part and I picked useDaySchedule because it holds the list state.
Whether RescheduleForm actually needs to change, or the rejection error should be shown elsewhere (e.g. a toast) — depends on the desired failure UX, which the request doesn't specify.

Where an automated test for the optimistic/rollback behavior should go: apps/web/tests/ only holds core/mappers tests (scheduling.core.test.ts) with no UI-composable precedent, so there's no established place for a composable-level test.

No data-layer change seems needed — mutations.ts already returns the updated Appointment and httpTransport throws HttpError on non-2xx (so rejection is detectable) — but I'm assuming no new Pinia store is warranted since the list is a per-view local ref, not shared cross-view cache.
questions: On server rejection after rollback, what exactly should the user see and where (inline form alert vs a global toast), and should the reschedule form reopen with their entered values?
During the optimistic window (before the server confirms), should conflict highlighting recompute live off the tentative time, or only after confirmation?
If the server accepts but returns a normalized time different from what was requested, should we reconcile the list to the server's value on success (replace the optimistic value)?
Should an in-flight optimistic change survive the user navigating away/back before the server responds — i.e. is per-view local state acceptable, or is shared/cached state (a store) expected here?

Is this optimistic pattern scheduling-specific for now, or should it be a reusable primitive (the billing slice has a similar cache store) — affects whether anything is generalized rather than kept inside scheduling/ui?
